tests.title: Visual-seed EAP end-to-end latency and utility

tests.title: Frank experience dose-response factorial
tests.question: At what amount of genuinely independent Frank-specific prior experience does memory coupling first produce a reproducible net benefit, how does that benefit scale, and when does it saturate or become harmful?
tests.experience_definition: One N unit is one independent provenance-bound Frank episode with visual/context evidence and verified outcome; repeated near-identical frames within one episode do not increase N. Qwen pretrained knowledge is constant and does not count as Frank experience.
tests.extend_rule: If benefit is still rising at 64 and independent data exist, continue geometrically to 128,256,... while useful.
tests.onset_rule: N_onset is the smallest tested N with reproducible net benefit over matched E0/no-experience without violating error/safety tolerances. A single favorable run does not count; inconclusive means N_onset > max_tested_N.
causal_controls: same Qwen model/runtime at every N
nested or matched stratified experience corpus

latency_language: Do not label EAP latency-free. Report measured end-to-end latency; microsecond-class subpaths may be negligible relative to 4B processing but are non-zero.
experience_language: Do not claim an experience effect from a binary familiar/unfamiliar comparison alone. Report the independent-episode dose-response curve and estimated onset/saturation/harm thresholds.
